paper_title: Extended Search for the Invisible Axion with the Axion Dark Matter Experiment
suggested_experiment_name: ADMX (Axion Dark Matter Experiment) - Extended Search 2018
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: ADMX haloscope cavity search excludes the full range of DFSZ axion-photon coupling (g_agamma ≈ 0.36 in natural units, corresponding to ~3.6e-16 GeV^-1) over the mass range 2.81–3.31 μeV. The paper reports 90% confidence exclusion limits on g_agamma as a function of axion mass in Fig. 4. The benchmark DFSZ coupling value is stated in Eq. (1) as g_γ = 0.36 (dimensionless). Converting to GeV^-1: g_agamma = 0.36 / (197.3 MeV·fm) ≈ 3.6e-16 GeV^-1 (using standard axion-photon coupling convention). The exclusion is mass-independent over the stated range (both Maxwell-Boltzmann and N-body halo models yield consistent limits). Local DM density of 0.45 GeV/cm³ is used in the analysis (stated in text and Eq. 1). This is the first ADMX result using a Josephson parametric amplifier and the first haloscope to fill mode crossings with alternate cavity configurations. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.92, 51)) | Vision: This is the ADMX 2018 extended search covering the mass range 2.81–3.31 μeV. The exclusion plot (FIG. 4) shows 90% confidence level limits on axion-photon coupling g_agamma as a function of axion mass. The x-axis is labeled in both frequency (MHz, bottom) and axion mass (μeV, top). The conversion between frequency and mass uses m[eV] = 4.136e-15 * f[Hz]. The lower boundary of the exclusion region (green shaded area labeled 'ADMX (This work)') is traced here. The plot also shows previous ADMX results (2010, orange), KSVZ and DFSZ benchmark model lines (black horizontal lines), and earlier constraints from other experiments. The boundary is relatively flat across most of the mass range at approximately 7.5–8.0 × 10^-15 GeV^-1, with a slight rise toward lower masses. The dark matter density assumed is ρ_a = 0.45 GeV/cm³ (standard galactic halo assumption). This work represents the first haloscope search to probe axions at mode crossings using an alternate cavity configuration, achieving unprecedented sensitivity in this higher mass range. | Calibration: No calibration needed (benchmark KSVZ raw_ratio=1.15 snapped to identity)
